filing_playbook.action: Meet with Planning Department pre-application team to confirm that a Type 42 license transferred from another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD will satisfy Planning Code § 249.60 for a CUA at 995 Valencia St.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request written confirmation that the SUD transfer requirement applies to this address and that the concept as described—beer-wine bar with limited food, live entertainment, 1 a.m. closing—will be classified as a Bar requiring CUA. Ask whether Planning has a list of transferable Type 42 licenses within the SUD or whether the applicant must source one independently. Confirm the CUA application can be filed before the license transfer is escrowed, or whether proof of an available license is a threshold requirement.

filing_playbook.action: Submit DPH plan check application for a bar with limited food preparation, including scaled drawings, equipment list, menu, and finishes schedule.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the concept is a bar use with a limited kitchen (no grease hood, only warming and assembly of prepared foods such as cheese, charcuterie, and small plates). Provide a menu showing the food offerings. Ask the DPH plan reviewer whether the existing kitchen equipment and finishes at 995 Valencia St (previously a restaurant) can be reused or must be upgraded.

timeline_cost.notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per the catalog) and the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60–150 days), which must be done sequentially or in parallel depending on Planning's confirmation that the CUA can be filed before the license is escrowed. The Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days) will run in parallel with the CUA or immediately after. Building permit plan review (14–120 days) and DPH plan check (21–60 days) typically overlap with the CUA hearing process. ABC's timeline may extend by 1–3 months (30–90 additional days) if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required due to the nine on-sale licenses within 500 ft. The minimum timeline assumes no PCN delay, over-the-counter DPH and building approvals, and a straightforward CUA hearing with no continuances (about 8 months total). The maximum timeline assumes a PCN referral, full plan review with revisions, a continued CUA hearing, and ABC transfer delays (about 19 months). Government fees include: CUA application (~$3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost, likely ~$3,100 for interior-only work), POE permit ($2,708), ABC Type 42 license ($1,000–$1,600 state fee, plus the market price of the license itself, which is not a government fee and is not included here), DPH plan check ($828–$2,500), Health Permit to Operate ($470), building permit ($800–$15,000, likely ~$3,000–$5,000 for bar build-out), SF Business Registration ($55–$700, likely ~$95), and state/federal registrations (EIN free, CA entity $70–$150, seller's permit free). Music licensing (ASCAP + BMI ~$600–$5,000/year) and workers' comp insurance are recurring costs, not one-time government fees, and are not included. The cost range reflects uncertainty in building permit fees (tied to construction valuation) and CUA fees (which escalate with project cost). The timeline and cost assume the operator can identify and escrow a transferable Type 42 license from a bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD; if no such license is available, no approval path exists and all figures are void.

status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the NCT-VALENCIA zoning district within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. The records classify the concept as a Bar (beer-wine service with live entertainment closing at 1 a.m.), which is a conditional use requiring CUA. The site currently operates as Sarita's Grill & Beer (restaurant) with an active Type 41 license issued November 2023; converting from Restaurant to Bar is a change of use. The block is densely activated: 24 food/drink businesses and 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with 51 total on-sale licenses within 1,000 ft—triggering ABC's undue-concentration test. Only 3 dated use decisions appear in the 10-year window nearby (1 approved, 2 withdrawn), too few for a meaningful approval rate, though 74 entertainment permits and licenses have been granted on Valencia and Mission corridors.
